newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish H1 Exchequer data distorted by timing factor.
newsitem.headline: Irish H1 Exchequer data distorted by timing factor.

text.p: Ireland's better-than-expected end-June Exchequer returns were distorted by the timing of value-added-tax and corporation tax receipts, finance ministry officials said on Wednesday.
"The figures are certainly very good but we would ask you to make some adjustments so we don't exaggerate the position," second secretary Michael Tutty told a news conference.

The Exchequer returns showed a surplus of 721 million Irish pounds in the first half of 1997, ahead of analysts' expectations of 100-650 million and a big improvement on the 455 million punt deficit recorded in the first half of 1996.

The finance ministry said the strength of tax receipts and lower-than-expected spending were the main reasons behind the higher-than-expected surplus but cautioned that both were due to timing factors.
Tutty said tax revenue grew by 23.5 percent in the six months to end-June but this was affected by the carryover of 119 million in VAT receipts from 1996.
The tax figures were also affected by corporation tax receipts which soared by 93.8 percent, mainly because receipts arrived in June this year compared with July last year.

But Tutty said that even adjusting for these factors, tax revenue was ahead of expectations, showing growth of 14.4 percent in the first half and the ministry expected tax revenue for the full-year to be about 500 million punts above the budget estimate.
Officials also cautioned that despite low year-on-year growth in spending in the first half, net current supply expenditure could exceed the budget target by 150 million punts for 1997 as a whole.

The main reasons for the overrun are an extra 70 million which is likely to be paid out in damages to sufferers of Hepatitis C, higher pay costs arising from settlement of a nurses' dispute, police and prison overtime and claims by soldiers suffering from deafness.
But even allowing for the overrun on spending, officials said they expected the Exchequer Borrowing Requirement for 1997 to be 300 to 400 million punts below the budget target of 637 million punts.
